title: Rabbi Joey Soffer: Mesilat Yesharim class #12

chapters.title: Introduction to Nikiut
chapters.about: Defining the attribute of nikiut and analyzing hidden sins.

chapters.title: The Difficulty of Hidden Sins
chapters.about: Why it is hard to identify sins when we have a desire to perform them.

chapters.title: Gezel and Rationalization
chapters.about: Discussing how people rationalize monetary theft and avak leshon hara.

chapters.title: David Hamelech and Purity
chapters.about: David Hamelech's confidence in his own purity before Hashem.

chapters.title: Details of Nikiut
chapters.about: The many subcategories of mitzvot lo taaseh.

chapters.title: Theft in Business
chapters.about: Common business practices that may violate laws of gezel.

chapters.title: Competition and Halakha
chapters.about: The Gemara in Bava Batra regarding business competition.

summary: Rabbi Soffer discusses the attribute of nikiut, the ability to analyze one's actions to identify and avoid hidden sins. He explains that people often rationalize their behavior, particularly in monetary matters and business, and emphasizes the importance of being objective to avoid falling into patterns of theft or improper conduct.
questions: How can I tell if I am making excuses for a sin?
Why is it harder to do teshuba for sins we don't recognize?
What does it mean to steal time from an employer?
Can a mitzvah be considered a sin if it is performed improperly?
How did David Hamelech maintain his purity?
